chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Uthman ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon him), who said:

My father, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), would stand at the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), send greetings upon him, testify to his delivery (of the Message), and supplicate with whatever came to his mind.

Then he would lean his back against the Marwah, the small, narrow green stone that faces the grave, press himself against the grave, lean his back against the grave, and face the Qiblah, saying: 'O Allah, to You I have turned my back for support, and to the grave of Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, I have leaned my back. And I have faced the Qiblah which You were pleased with for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

O Allah, I have become such that I do not possess for myself any of the good I hope for, nor do I repel from it any of the evil I fear for it. And the affairs have come to be in Your Hand, so there is no poor one poorer than I. Indeed, I am poor for whatever good You send down to me. O Allah, return me to You with goodness, for there is none who can repel Your Grace. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from my name being changed, or my body being altered, or Your Bounties being removed from me. O Allah, honor me with Taqwa (piety), adorn me with Bounties, immerse me in Al-Afiyah (health/wholeness), and grant me Shukr (gratitude) for Al-Afiyah.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when leaning against the Marwah at the Prophet's grave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the devotional etiquette of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) during Ziyarah, emphasizing the physical act of leaning against the Marwah stone as a sign of reliance upon the Prophet's intercession. The supplication reflects the Shia theological emphasis on human insufficiency (*faqir*) and the necessity of seeking divine facilitation (*rad al-fadl*) through the Prophet's grave, linking the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt with the ultimate source of all grace.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Husayn Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Hassan Bin Ali Bin Usman Bin Ali, son of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother Al-Hassan Bin Musa<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> brother, from his grandfather<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>

would pause at the grave of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> would greet upon him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> would testify to him<sup>saww</sup> with the delivery (of the Message), and supplicate with what presented to him<sup>asws</sup>.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> would incline his<sup>asws</sup> back towards the green rock displayed on the ground from what follows the grave, and he<sup>asws</sup> would incline his<sup>asws</sup> back towards the grave, and he<sup>asws</sup> would face the Qiblah and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘To You<sup>azwj</sup> I<sup>asws</sup> I seek Support of my<sup>asws</sup> back, and to the grave of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>. I<sup>asws</sup> incline my<sup>asws</sup> back and the Qiblah which Your<sup>azwj</sup> were Pleased with Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> have I<sup>asws</sup> turned towards.

O Allahazwj! Iasws have become such that Iasws do not possess good for myselfasws what Iasws hope for, nor repelling evil what Iasws am cautious over, and the affairs have come to be in Yourazwj Hands. Thus, there is no poor one poorer than Iasws am. [28:24] Surely I stand in need of whatever good You may Send down upon me. O Allahazwj! Iasws intend to be Returned from Youazwj with goodness, for there is none who can repel Yourazwj Grace. O Allahazwj! Iasws seek Refuge from myasws name being changed, or myasws body being altered, or Yourazwj Bounties to decline from measws. O Allahazwj! Be Generous on measws with the piety, and Load upon measws with the Bounties, and Immerse measws in the good health, and Grace measws the thankfulness for the good health’’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Kufiy from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn ‘Uthman from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn abu Talib from Ali ibn Ja’far who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his father from his grandfather, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, this Hadith.

‘My father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would stand near the grave of the Holy Prophet and offer his Salam, testify to his preaching the messages of Allah and ask Allah for his wishes, as he wanted.

He then liked to keep his back against the brightly green stone, which is next to the grave, stay attached to the grave with his back toward it, facing the direction of Ka’bah, and say, “O Allah, I have sought backing and support from You. I have turned my back for support toward the grave of Muhammad, Your servant and Your messenger, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. I have set my back for support and faced the direction, which You chose for Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.

O Allah, I do not possess anything good for myself that I can hope for. I am not able to keep away from my soul any evil and wickedness of which I am afraid. All matters are in Your hands. There is no one poorer than I am. I am in dire need of goodness because of what has come upon me. O Allah, return me back with goodness; no one is able to keep away Your favors. O Allah, I seek protection with You against Your changing my name, my body and removal of Your bounties from me. O Allah, honor me with piety, beautify me with bounties, cover me with good health and grant me the opportunity to thank you for good health.’””
